rule: A 3-cell grey (5) bar with a 9 touching its middle forms a gun. The ray starts at the 9, passes through the bar centre and continues to the grid edge. Every 4-connected yellow (4) blob the ray touches is erased to the background colour 7.
scope: Supported: random grid sizes 8..30 per side, horizontal or vertical bars, the 9 on either side (all four firing directions), random 4-connected blobs of 1..20 cells with size-dependent maximum at about 14-24% density, 1-3 blobs on the firing line, and many off-line distractors. Distractors can touch line blobs diagonally or touch the bar. Not supported: bar lengths other than 3, other colours, multiple guns, or a background other than 7. These stay fixed, matching the original task.
constraints: Exactly one 9 and one 3-cell 5 bar; the 9 is orthogonally adjacent to the bar centre on its perpendicular side.
Yellow cells never overlap the bar or the 9.
Separately grown random blobs are never 4-adjacent to each other, so blob identity is exactly the planned shapes; diagonal contact is allowed.
At least one yellow cell lies on the ray beyond the bar, so the output is never the identity.
At least 3 yellow cells survive, so the scene always has distractors.
The ray runs from the 9 away from it through the bar only; cells behind the 9 are not affected.
The output is computed from the 4-connected components of the yellow-cell set.
known_limitations: Colours and the bar length are fixed, as in the original task.
Fixture reconstruction passes the yellow layout as a pattern of strings rather than as individual blob objects; blobs are recovered as its 4-connected components.
Randomly grown blobs are not 4-adjacent to each other, while the original grids can contain larger irregular merged clusters.
Larger canvases and blob-size maxima extend the original scale; no difficulty equivalence is claimed.
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback
